title: MatchRequest
description: A person's request to find what they have in common with other people — what they could talk about or do together. The request itself is written on the requester's own vault by the application they asked in, acting for them; its audience names the services the requester wants to answer, and a service not in it should not. That application may also put a reference to the request on the vault of each such service, as a signal that a request for it exists; a reference carries no copy of the request, and the service reads the request itself from canonicalOwnerEName's vault. Answers are MatchSuggestion records that reference the request. Immutable: a changed request is a new record that supersedes this one.

isReference.description: true on a reference to a request, kept on the vault of a service asked to answer it; absent or false on the request itself

id.description: Stable id chosen by the writer when the request is made; a reference carries the id of the request it refers to. Not the envelope id, which the vault assigns; references to the record use the envelope URI

requester.description: The person asking. On the request itself, the owner of the vault it is on

people.description: Everyone between whom common ground is to be found, the requester included when they ask about themselves

purpose.description: What the requester hopes to find, in their own words, when they said

language.description: BCP-47 tag of the language the requester wants the answer in

supersedes.description: An earlier request of the same requester that this one replaces

createdAt.description: When the record was written, RFC 3339

canonicalOwnerEName.description: On a reference: the requester, whose vault holds the request

canonicalEnvelopeId.description: On a reference: the envelope id of the request on canonicalOwnerEName's vault

sharedBy.description: On a reference: who put it there — the requester, through the application acting for them

sharedAt.description: On a reference: when it was put there, RFC 3339
